passages.text: Podocarpus acutifolius, commonly known as needle-leaved tōtara, is a species of conifer in the family Podocarpaceae. This species is endemic to New Zealand.

Etymology 
The specific epithet, {{lang|la|acutifolius}}, meaning "thorny leaves", is derived from Latin {{lang|la|acutus}} (pointed, acute), and {{lang|la|-folius}} (-leaved), and refers to the characteristic shape of the leaves.

Distribution 
This species is found in the South Island from northern Marlborough westward and south to southern Westland. Its natural habitat is lowland and montane forest and scrub.
